# Conductor API contract v1

These files are the truth for `/v1/conductor/*` (server/conductor/routes.py). The server's tests validate real responses against them (`tests/test_conductor_e2e.py`), and the dashboard's mock engine validates its fixtures and every mock response (`dashboard/tests/conductor-contract.test.ts`). They live beside `dashboard-v1` rather than inside it so the two contracts can change on their own.

| file | endpoint |
|-|-|
| `config.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/config`: loaded versions, load errors, the journal |
| `meta.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/meta`: enums, the task catalogue with units, the schemas |
| `profiles.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/profiles`: the tiles |
| `document.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/{settings,router,roles,packages}`, `GET /v1/conductor/profiles/{name}` |
| `write.schema.json` | `PUT` of a document, `POST .../restore`, `POST /v1/conductor/profiles/{name}/mode` |
| `versions.schema.json` | `GET .../versions` |
| `diff.schema.json` | `GET .../diff?from=&to=` |
| `roles.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/roles`: the document and each role's health |
| `role-test.schema.json` | `POST /v1/conductor/roles/{role}/test` |
| `classify.schema.json` | `POST /v1/conductor/classify`: the test box |
| `decisions.schema.json`, `decision.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/decisions`, `GET /v1/conductor/decisions/{id}`; `$defs` holds one router decision (with `events`, the monitor's decisions in the same request) and one monitor event |
| `events.schema.json`, `event.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/events?task=&mode=&acted=&session=`, `GET /v1/conductor/events/{id}`: the session monitor's decisions |
| `stats.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/stats?hours=` |
| `sessions.schema.json`, `session.schema.json`, `export.schema.json` | the session list, one timeline, the JSON export |
| `evals.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/evals`: reports in the config directory's `evals/` (a suite report's own schema is `dashboard-v1/tandem-eval.schema.json`; a `speed_guard` report is written by `tools/speed_guard.py`: `build`, `base` and `cand` (label, runs, code), `runs_each`, `noise_estimated`, `stats` (per statistic `base`, `cand`, `delta_pct`, `noise_pct` or null), `verdict` `pass`, `worse` or `no_noise_estimate`, `why`) |
| `eval-write.schema.json` | `POST /v1/conductor/evals` `{report}`: a suite report from `tools/tandem_eval.py` kept in `evals/` (the admin rule; 422 when it lacks `kind` suite, `night` or rows with `suite` and `arm`) |
| `watch.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/watch`: the session tasks' state per session (S1's gates, S2's compaction watch, S4's progress and the idle client) |
| `residency-plan.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/residency/plan` (OPS-41): the residency document, what may load beside the engine now, the engine's memory split, the planner's journal; the document itself is `GET`/`PUT /v1/conductor/residency` like the others |
| `deciders-status.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/deciders/status` (SRV-131): the decision models this engine serves, each with its state and numbers, the residency planner's answer for a load now, the last refused engine load, the model behind each question id and what `auto` picked; `enabled: false` with `why` when `QWEN38_DECIDER_MODELS` is empty. The `deciders` document itself is `GET`/`PUT /v1/conductor/deciders` like the others |
| `decider-action.schema.json` | `POST /v1/conductor/deciders/models/{name}/load` (202, or 409 with the planner's decision), `.../unload` (200; 409 when not loaded), `POST /v1/conductor/deciders/autoload` (202, `queued`: the `on_start` models; what `ops/start.sh` asks for) |
| `systemone.schema.json` | `POST /v1/conductor/deciders/test` (the test box, the dashboard's rule) and the engine's own `POST /v1/systemone` and `/v1/predict` (the `decider` auth rule): one Jev answer object per question |
| `laya-ask.schema.json`, `laya-ask-texts.schema.json` | `POST /v1/laya/ask` (L1, anyone as the chat API): Laya's typed answer for the model's own scripts, one text (with `model` and `ms`) or `texts` (`answers`, one a text). Errors have the OpenAI shape. The `deciders` document's `api` section configures it and `GET /v1/conductor/deciders/status` reports it as `api` |
| `library.schema.json`, `library-search.schema.json`, `library-skill.schema.json` | `GET /v1/library`, `GET /v1/library/search?q=&k=&class=`, `GET /v1/library/{name}` (R1, anyone as the chat API): the package library's enabled skills, a search's best skills first (`[]` when no word matches), one skill's injected text and its reference. Errors have the OpenAI shape. A profile's `library` switch and the router's `library` section configure the router's own retrieval |
| `memory-sessions.schema.json`, `memory-session.schema.json`, `memory-keep.schema.json` | VIS-48, SRV-137: `GET /v1/conductor/memory/sessions` (every session transcript on the box with its meta.json, and the writer's counters and settings), `GET /v1/conductor/memory/sessions/{key}?page=N` (its blocks, 200 a page, the newest page by default, read to the last complete block) and `.../export?format=json` (every block; `format=md` is the file itself), `PATCH .../keep {keep}`. Every memory route needs the admin token, a dashboard session or the box itself, reads included |
| `memory-disk.schema.json`, `memory-disk-clear.schema.json` | C1: `GET /v1/conductor/memory/disk` (the disk tier: whether it runs, its settings and their version, its bytes against the budget and the free space against the 50 GB floor, the hit rate, the 20 most-hit entries -- a preview only for opencode heads and packages -- and its last events) and `POST /v1/conductor/memory/disk/clear` (what was on disk before, and the tier after; 409 when it does not run). Admin token, like every memory route |
| `scan.schema.json` | `GET /v1/conductor/packages/scan` |
| `packages-catalog.schema.json`, `packages-item.schema.json`, `packages-tokens.schema.json`, `packages-usage.schema.json` | G2, the Packages and Skills screen's reads: `GET /v1/conductor/packages/catalog` (every package: category, source and path, the tokens of the text that goes in on the engine's tokenizer or the 3.5-character estimate, its limit and whether it is over, the classes of the router and of each profile that list it, INDEX.md's fit, each profile's library switch), `GET /v1/conductor/packages/item/{name}` (frontmatter, body, reference, the text that goes in, their tokens, a library skill's BM25 neighbours; 404 for an unknown name), `POST /v1/conductor/packages/tokens {texts}` (a read: the tokens of 1 to 20 texts; 400 otherwise), `GET /v1/conductor/packages/usage?name=&limit=` (the journal's 7 days: per package its injections, shadow notes and library picks in 24 h and 7 d, one package's newest rows, the library's newest retrieval rows; 400 for a limit outside 1 to 200) |
| `error.schema.json` | every 4xx body; a 422 adds `errors` with one line per violation and its JSON path |
| `<kind>.config.schema.json` | the documents themselves; written from server/conductor/schema.py by `tools/conductor_contract.py --write` |
| `seeds.json` | the built-in version 0 of every document and the meta; the mock engine serves it |

Rules the schemas cannot express, which both sides test:

- A write needs a one-line note (422 without one). `base_version` is optional; when it is sent and the document moved on since, the answer is 409. `raw` and `bench` answer 409 to every write.
- A `PUT` that fails validation answers 422 and leaves the current version as it was. `POST .../check` runs the same validation without writing and returns the diff against the live version.
- A profile whose Tier 1 task is set to `act` while that task's role is offline is refused with the reason.
- `stats.precision` counts, per profile and decision type that ran in shadow, the decisions a person labelled and how many were right; the dashboard allows "Promote to on" at precision 0.9 or more over 30 or more labelled decisions.

## Changes

- v1.0, first version.
- v1.0, SRV-113/115, additive: one journal for the router and the session monitor. The `monitor` document (the monitor's policy; its schema is the policy's own, a branch per rule, and version 0 is the server's `ops/supervisor.yaml`). `events` and `event`. A router row gains the journal's common fields (`kind`, `task`, `tier`, `decision`, `action`, `trigger`, `score`, `tier1_model`, `question_id`, `probabilities`, `tier1_ms`, `hidden_text_id`, `hidden_tokens`, `position`, ...) and `events`; `session` gains `events`; `sessions` gains `acts`, `gave_ups`, `shadow` and `interventions`; `stats.monitor` is the monitor's block (null when no monitor runs); the export lists every intervention of either half (`source` router or monitor) with its exact text and says `summary`, "N interventions in M turns". A label (`POST .../decisions/{id}/label`) takes any row's id. `config.journal` names the ledger's file.
- v1.0, SRV-121 and OPS-43, additive: `GET /v1/conductor/watch` (the session tasks' state per session) and `POST /v1/conductor/evals` (a suite report kept for the Compare screen). The `monitor` document gains the session tasks S2 (`context_health`), S1 (`gate_stagnation`) and S4 (`stall_watchdog`, with its `notify` block); a monitor event from the watch has `sp` `watch` (S4's `client_gone`, `decision` PASS, or NOTIFY when its push is enabled). A profile's `context` (`s1_runs`, `s4_minutes`, `notify`) sets S1's `fails`, S4's `minutes` and `notify.enabled`.
- v1.0, OPS-41, additive: the `residency` document (the planner's floor, margin, settle time, load order and each role's memory claim with its basis), `GET /v1/conductor/residency/plan`, and `residency` in `config.store.documents`.
- v1.0, additive: the `monitor` document's C2 (`project_rules`) takes `allow_paths`, the paths no C2 rule applies to (default `/tmp/opencode`; left out, the default applies). A `speed_guard` report in `evals/` (`tools/speed_guard.py`) carries the row pair's numbers and a verdict; one run a side is `no_noise_estimate`.
- v1.0, SRV-131, additive: the `deciders` document (each decision model's load policy, `on_start`, `on_demand` or `off`, and the model behind each question id, `classify` and `packages` today), `GET /v1/conductor/deciders/status`, `POST /v1/conductor/deciders/models/{name}/load|unload`, `POST /v1/conductor/deciders/autoload`, `POST /v1/conductor/deciders/test`, and `deciders` in `config.store.documents`. The `roles` seed's `decider` is `endpoint: self` (the engine's own decision models, asked in process) instead of the :8010 sidecar.
- v1.0, OPS-47, additive: the `residency` document gains `engine`, the engine's memory limits the dashboard overrides by their serve.env names (`MEM_CEILING_GIB`, `MEM_PEAK_GIB`, `RESERVE_SLACK_GIB`, `RESIDENT_GB`, `RESIDENT_STASH_GB`, `RESIDENT_GUEST_MAX`, `RESIDENT_PIN_GB`, `RESIDENT_PARK_GB`, `CACHE_GB`, `STORE_ENTRY_GB`, `VISION_EMBED_MB`, `SUFFIX_STORE_MB`, `PREFIX_CHUNK`, `NARROW_ARM`; never `MAX_LEN`), and the planner counts the engine's growth to its declared peak before a claim: a check, a plan row and the plan gain `engine_peak_gib`, `engine_now_gib` and `engine_growth_gib`, and `after_gib` is MemAvailable less that growth less the claim. `GET /v1/conductor/residency/plan` gains `limits` (every limit, what it holds now, the shed log, the last session switch), and the journal gains the engine's memory lines (`memory_shed`, `memory_refused`, `memory_estimate_raised`, role `engine`).
- v1.0, SRV-133, a rename and additions: a role in the `roles` document carries the role contract -- `kind` (reasoner, decider, probe, clerk, librarian, tool), `memory_claim_gib` (was `memory_gb`), `window` (idle, in_decode, any), `preemptible`, `latency_budget_ms`, `fallback` (PASS, stale, skip, next-role), `tokenizer_sha256` (64 hex characters or `none`), `writes` (client_visible, hidden_notes, memory_files, nothing) and `sharing` (text, tokens, states) -- every one required on a write. Rules: `writes: client_visible` only for kind reasoner; `window: in_decode` only for a decider or a probe; `sharing: states` only for a probe; `sharing: tokens` only with the engine's own tokenizer hash. A version stored before the contract loads with defaults (`memory_gb` becomes `memory_claim_gib`, `latency_budget_ms` the role's `timeout_ms`, `kind` from the role's name or contract, then window idle, preemptible true, fallback PASS, writes nothing, tokenizer none, sharing text), listed in the document's `meta.defaults` and journaled (`kind` config); a restore of such a version writes it whole. `GET /v1/conductor/roles` gains `contract` (the engine's tokenizer hash; per role the forms of sharing it may use and whether its hash is the engine's); the meta gains `roles` (the contract's values); a decision model in `deciders/status` gains `role`, the contract it signs, which the registry checks before it serves the model.
- v1.0, SRV-137 and VIS-48, additive: the `settings` document gains `memory.transcripts` (`scope` tools, all or none; `retention_days`; `clip_chars`; `loop_chars`; left out, the defaults apply), the memory routes above, and the JSON export of a session gains `transcript` (the block count and the memory export's path, or null). The journal gains rows of `kind` memory (a block's redaction counts per kind, never a value; a failed write; the prune; a keep) and `kind` config.
- v1.0, C1, additive: the `settings` document gains `memory.disk_cache` (`mode` on or off, `budget_gb`, `ttl_days`, `admit_after`, `min_free_gb` of at least 50; left out, the defaults 50 GB, 7 days, 2, 50 GB apply), the two disk routes above, and the journal gains rows of `kind` memory, `task` disk_cache (`decision` hit, write, evict, drop, restore_failed, clear, error; counts, token lengths and reasons, never a text).
- v1.0, S1 (2026-10-02), additive: the `router` document's `structural` gains `side_requests` (`on`, `off`; left out, on) and `side_shapes` (a list of `{id, client, kind: title|summary, match, max_tokens}` that replaces the built-in shapes of a client's side requests); a profile's `ui` gains `states_channel` (`reasoning`, `content`; left out, reasoning) and `progress` (`{mode, prefill_every_s, thinking_every_s, thinking_every_tokens}`; left out, on with the defaults), and `ui.kinds` names `queue`, `prefill` and `thinking`. A router row's `kind` may be `side` (a client's side request served by its shape: `decision` the shape, `action` `SIDE_REQUEST`, `cap` its output cap, `extra.side`); `GET /v1/conductor/decisions` lists the side rows with the router's turns; `stats`, `sessions` and a session's turns read the turns alone. The meta gains `state_channels` and `side_kinds`. A version saved with any of these keys is refused by a server before S1, which serves the newest older version.
- v1.0, G2 (2026-10-03), additive: `GET /v1/conductor/packages/catalog`, `GET /v1/conductor/packages/item/{name}`, `POST /v1/conductor/packages/tokens` and `GET /v1/conductor/packages/usage`, all reads under the dashboard's rule; no document and no journal row changes.
- v1.0, X1 (2026-10-03), additive: a profile's `ui.states_channel` may be `inline` (each state line the title of a reasoning part of its own: an empty `tool_calls` delta, then a reasoning delta `\n**› text**\n\n`; on a `reasoning_content` stream only, `content` otherwise); the meta's `state_channels` lists it. The `deciders` document's `api` gains `drive_rate_per_s`, `drive_sessions`, `drive_idle_s` and `drive_max_texts` (left out, 10, 4, 30, 36,000); `POST /v1/laya/ask` takes an optional `session` (a driver session: its own rate, no journal row a call; the answer is unchanged), `POST /v1/laya/drive/end {session, summary?}` answers the session's numbers and writes one journal row (`kind` laya_drive, `task` session, `decision` end or idle), `GET /v1/laya/kit/<file>` serves the playtest kit (`laya_drive.py`, `laya-drive.js`) as text; `deciders-status`'s `api` gains the four limits and `stats.drive_sessions`. A version saved with these keys is refused by a server before X1.
